issues.description: The solution's assembleBookstore function signature does not match the template/problem expectation. The problem statement (and the commented prototype in the template) expect a zero-argument function: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore, and Client.main() calls assembleBookstore() with no arguments. In the solution the function is implemented as private static func assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore (i.e. it requires a Bool parameter) while main() still calls assembleBookstore() without an argument. This mismatch will cause a compile-time error and is inconsistent with the template and problem specification, which is likely to confuse students and break the provided example solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's assembleBookstore function signature match the problem/template by removing the parameter. Change the solution to: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so that the existing call in main() (assembleBookstore()) compiles. Alternatively, if a parameter is intentionally required, update the problem statement/template and the call site in main() to pass an appropriate argument — however, removing the unused parameter in the solution is the simpler fix and preserves the intended exercise API.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument function named `assembleBookstore()` that returns a `Bookstore`. In the solution repository the same conceptual function is defined as `assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore` (introducing a parameter named `check`) which is not mentioned in the problem or template. This divergence (an extra parameter identifier) creates a mapping confusion: students will implement or look for a no-argument `assembleBookstore()` as requested, while the solution's definition introduces an unexpected parameter name and signature mismatch.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function signature consistent across artifacts. Remove the extraneous parameter from the solution so the function is `private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore` (and ensure calls use no arguments). Alternatively, if a parameter is required intentionally, update the problem statement and template to document the parameter name and purpose and provide a default value so calls without arguments remain valid. The recommended fix is to remove the `check: Bool` parameter from the solution to match the exercise specification.
